intent: new execution of existing T-E concept
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: original transparent front-print T-shirt artwork for adult antique/vintage treasure hunters, a typography-led quiet dry-humor variant.
Create a polished, restrained composition in ONE solid warm ivory ink (#F2E4C7) on a truly transparent background. No shirt, no rectangle/background, no shadows, no mockup.
Exact wording, verbatim:
DO YOU
DELIVER?
I asked, after paying.
The first two lines are the leading typographic element: well-spaced medium-weight classic book serif capitals, dignified and slightly wry, not heavy block or rounded cartoon lettering. Treat DO YOU and DELIVER? as one question with deliberate line rhythm. Below them place the complete sentence "I asked, after paying." in a smaller plain readable serif, on ONE line, with visible breathing room. The punchline must remain easily readable; do not make it a tiny disclaimer. Keep it approximately half the cap height of the question letters.
Below the copy, with a generous but coherent gap, center one SMALL isolated antique two-door sideboard/cabinet vignette, approximately 28–32% of the total typography width. The cabinet has old-fashioned raised-panel doors, one top drawer, modest decorative top and turned short feet, with a clearly shaped blank string-hung dealer tag on one knob. One-ink simplified line illustration with open transparent interiors and robust clean strokes. Distinctive silhouette, minimal interior detail: it must read as old furniture even at modest size. This small object is a supporting treasure-hunting cue, not a hero illustration. NO car, no person, no extra objects, no extra words or price, no badge/frame, no flourishes, no excessive distress. No outline around letters. Match clean ivory strokes throughout.
Overall graphic is calm and compact, about as wide as tall or slightly wider, with plenty of transparent outer margin. A quiet statement with an object footnote, not a dense typographic poster. Flat screen-print-like opaque ink, sharp edges, correct apostrophe, question mark, comma and period.
